title: An Efficient and Reproducible Protocol for Distraction Osteogenesis in a Rat Model Leading to a Functional Regenerated Femur
protocol: Implant half-threaded pins with a diameter of the threaded section of 1 mm for optimal bone anchorage.
Choose an external fixator design that minimizes discomfort for the animal.
Select an external fixator small enough to fit into a volume of 7,723 mm³ (32 mm x 19 mm x 12.7 mm).
Ensure the external fixator weighs less than 13 g without pins to avoid disturbing the animals' gait.
Use aluminum as the material for the two blocks due to its low density.
Incorporate chamfers on the blocks to reduce their weight.
Control motion of the fixator to maintain tensile force parallel to bone direction.
Implement a sliding bar that passes through both blocks.
Groove and open the blocks so each can bear two pins.
Use an elongation screw with one smooth and free-turning side and a threaded side.
Anchor two pins on each side of the fracture in the bone.
Maintain tensile forces along the longitudinal axis of the bone.
Secure the four pins using locking screws.
Choose materials such as aluminum, titanium, or steel for the components.
Ensure pin placement aligns with external fixator geometry.
Use a drilling guide clamped to the bone to maintain drilling position.
Shorten the lever arm of the clamp for low clamping force.
Position the clamp in the middle of the device above the future fracture site.
Add a knurled screw to adjust distraction manually and easily.
Ensure the screw is wide enough to manipulate with fingers alone.
Insert a drilled square nut between the two blocks on the elongation screw.
Make the square nut (8 mm on each side) larger than the blocks for manual use.
Turn the screw ¼ turn to allow a lengthening of 0.125 mm.
Prepare surgical tools.
Sterilize 1 rugine.
Sterilize 2 Senn's retractors.
Sterilize 1 micro Olsen-Hegar Needle-holder.
Sterilize 1 Mayo-Hegar needle holder.
Sterilize 1 mayo scissor.
Sterilize 1 scalpel.
Sterilize an external fixator.
Sterilize a drilling guide.
Sterilize 4 half-threaded pins.
Sterilize 4 screws.
Sterilize the tip and string of the drill.
Sterilize the tip and string of the piezotome.
Install a heating pad below the sterile field on the surgical table.
Place all instruments or tools on another sterile field.
Weigh the rat to prepare the anesthetic and analgesic mixture.
Calculate the amount of Buprenorphine for the analgesic mixture.
Calculate the amount of Carprofen for the analgesic mixture.
Restrain the rat and subcutaneously inject the analgesic mixture.
Wait a few seconds, then inject intraperitoneally the anesthetic mixture.
Shave the right hind limb with an electric razor.
Disinfect the limb with povidone-iodine solution.
Lay the animal laterally (right side upward) on the sterile field to allow correct positioning of the external fixator along the mediolateral axis.
Put a sterile compress on its head to protect its eyes during surgery.
Implant the external fixator in the femur.
Landmark the skin incision.
Draw a point from the distal part (knee) and a second point in the proximal part (hip) following the median line in the sagittal plane.
Draw a line between these two points.
Incise the stretched skin along the drawing line using a scalpel.
Cut in between the biceps femoris and vastus lateralis until the femur is fully exposed, with the help of a scalpel.
Use 2 Senn's retractors to facilitate muscle incision.
Lift the periosteum and disconnect the soft tissue from the bone with the help of a rugine.
Check that the exposed femur is long enough.
Insert pins in the most proximal and distal holes of the external fixator.
Position the external fixator and check that both pins can be anchored into the femur.
Take the drilling guide and move apart the muscles with 2 Senn's retractors.
Tighten the clamp of the drilling guide in the middle of the femur.
Drill 4 pre-holes in the femur using an electric drill at a speed of 2,000 rpm by passing a metal drill bit of 0.6 mm diameter through the 4 guide holes.
Start with the most proximal and distal holes and finish with the two middle ones of the guide.
Be careful to go through both cortices but not to damage the soft tissues just beneath the femur.
Take off the drilling guide.
Enlarge the 4 pre-holes with 0.8 mm half-threaded pin.
Work the pin back and forth through the 0.6 mm holes.
Ensure the pin stays perpendicular to the femur and sinks through both cortices.
Implant a 1 mm half-threaded pin.
Grip the head of the 1 mm half-threaded pin with a needle-holder.
Sink the pin to enlarge the pre-hole.
Check that pins penetrate both cortices and do not protrude more than 1 mm.
Connect the external fixator to the 4 half-threaded pins.
Ensure the offset is about 6 mm for easy stitches and good rigidity of the system.
Secure the 4 locking screws to lock the external fixator to the pins.
Osteotomize the femur using a piezotome between the two central pins.
Close the wound with a continuous stitch using a resorbable suture thread (5.0) and Mayo-Hegar needle holder.
Ensure only the skin is stitched, not the muscles.
Perform an X-ray while the animal is still anesthetized to verify surgery details.
Check the depth of all pins and alignment of osteotomized extremities following the long axis.
Ensure analgesia and antibioprophylaxis by subcutaneous injection of Buprenorphine at 0.03 mg/mL.
Administer Enrofloxacine at 50 mg/mL subcutaneously.
Calculate the amount of Antipamezole to reverse anesthesia.
Inject Antipamezole at 1mg/kg subcutaneously.
Allow the animal to regain consciousness and return it to its cage.
Six hours post-surgery, inject a second dose of analgesia mixture (Buprenorphine at 0.05 mg/kg and Carprofen at 5 mg/kg) subcutaneously.
For the next three days, administer the analgesia mixture twice daily and antibioprophylaxy once daily.
Perform regular clinical examinations to assess analgesia effectiveness based on animal behavior signs.
Check that animals can walk using their operated hind limb normally the day following surgery.
Leave the external fixator in neutral fixation for one week.
X-ray the limb at the end of this phase.
Manually turn the square nut one half turn (0.25 mm) clockwise every 12 hours to perform distraction.
Distract for ten days, leading to a 5mm bone lengthening relative to the initial length of the operated bone segment.
Do not anesthetize the animal during this step.
X-ray the limb halfway through and at the end of the period to check the positioning of the pins and alignment of the bone segments.
Maintain the external fixator for 47 days.
X-ray the limb weekly to check the progress of distracted gap calcification.
On Day 64, remove the external fixator and let the animal walk freely for 2 more days (Day 66).
Euthanize all rats after 7 weeks of consolidation with an overdose of inhaled sevoflurane.
Make a skin incision on the scar located on the median line following the sagittal plane with the help of a scalpel.
Run the incision from the top of the hip to the front of the knee.
Cut between the biceps femoris and vastus lateralis with a scalpel until the femur is fully exposed.
Disconnect as much muscle attached to the bone as possible.
Cut all ligaments of the knee and dismantle the articulation.
Cut the joint capsule of the hip.
Clean the bone thoroughly without removing the half-threaded pins.
Remove all soft tissue with a scalpel.
Repeat steps from 3.5.1 to 3.5.5 for the contralateral femur.
X-ray distracted and contralateral femurs.
Remove the 4 half-threaded pins.
Store all femurs at -20°C for micro-CT scan analysis (10 µm resolution).
